tools.name: resolve_entity
tools.description: Map an organization name (a contract recipient, a subsidiary, a PAC sponsor, a Form D issuer) to its public-company ticker. Exact normalized match against SEC legal names, aliases and the Exhibit 21 subsidiary map; returns the method and a confidence, or the reason for a miss. Never guesses.

tools.name: get_entity
tools.description: One company in the federal record: contracts won, PACs, patents, private raises, members of Congress who hold board seats there, insider trades, and its connections graph. Look up by ticker, entity_id, or a name (resolved exactly).

name.description: Company name; resolved by exact match

tools.name: search_awards
tools.description: Search federal contract awards (USAspending, $10M+) by recipient, ticker, awarding agency, keyword, date range or minimum amount. Returns total_matching and pages with offset (up to 50 per call), sorted by date or amount. Each award's amount is its lifetime value, not money obligated in the dates asked; never add them up as a period total.

keyword.description: Word in the award description or NAICS description

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

until.description: ISO date; only rows on or before this date

tools.name: award_totals
tools.description: Verified totals of money obligated in the dates asked, per recipient or agency, where verified figures are available. Where they are not, it says so, gives no total, and lists the largest matching awards with their lifetime values labelled. Never present a lifetime value or a sum of them as a period total.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

until.description: ISO date; only rows on or before this date

tools.name: contract_vehicles
tools.description: The ways the government buys: contract vehicles from the verified award records, with who holds them, the agency, industry and set-aside, status (open, expired, cancelled, terminated, closed out), the ordering-period end, and their history (new, extensions, ceiling changes, options, cancellations, corrections). Pass vehicle_key for one vehicle with the orders placed on it, or search by query words, ticker (verified contractor IDs only), uei, agency, status=open|closed or ending_before. MONEY IS KEPT APART: ceiling is the most that may be ordered, NEVER money awarded or obligated, and ceilings must never be added together (multiple-award vehicles repeat one program ceiling for every awardee); obligated_on_orders is money actually obligated on orders placed on the vehicle in verified years; remaining_capacity is null unless it can be stated soundly (single-award vehicle, whole order history held). Quote these labels when you summarise.

query.description: Words in the vehicle description, program name, holder or industry

ticker.description: Holder ticker; matched through verified contractor IDs only

ending_before.description: ISO date; vehicles whose ordering period ends on or before it (recompetes)

tools.name: search_opportunities
tools.description: Search SAM.gov notices: Sources Sought and Pre-solicitations (the earliest public signal of a purchase), solicitations and combined synopses. Filter by keyword, NAICS, agency, notice type, date. Each result carries hillsignal_url, the HillSignal opportunity page (notice history, typical time to award, who won similar work, competitors' lobbying and PAC money); give that link to the user, with ui_link as the SAM.gov source. For the full analysis of one notice, call get_opportunity with its hillsignal_url.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

tools.name: get_opportunity
tools.description: One SAM.gov notice as HillSignal analyses it: its history under the solicitation number, when the award usually comes, who won similar work (with matched_by saying how: same office and product/service code is tightest) and the spread of their award sizes, listed winners' revenue for scale with an investor_context line, competitors' lobbying at the agency (dollar totals are filing totals across every issue on them), lobbyists' past jobs there, PAC money to the overseeing committees, insider buys and sells with how many sales were under a 10b5-1 plan, and related bills, rules and orders. Pass id from search_opportunities (hillsignal_url or its id) or a SAM.gov notice id. Quote matched_by and the notes when you summarise.

id.description: HillSignal opportunity id or page url, or a SAM.gov notice id

tools.name: congressional_trades
tools.description: Stock trades disclosed by members of Congress (House and Senate Periodic Transaction Reports), by member name, ticker, transaction type or date. Returns one row per transaction with the disclosed amount range and the filing PDF. limit caps the FILINGS read, not the trades returned, and filings_matching is how many exist: when truncated is set, far more trades exist than are shown and returned_trades must never be quoted as a total.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

tools.name: get_politician
tools.description: A member of Congress: committees, board seats and other positions from annual Financial Disclosures (with resolved tickers), recent stock trades, and top PAC contributors from FEC data. Look up by name or bioguide_id; ambiguous names return candidates.

tools.name: insider_trades
tools.description: SEC Form 4 insider transactions by ticker or insider name; filter to buys or sells, minimum value, date.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

tools.name: search_bills
tools.description: Full-text search over bills, contract awards and other government events with their analysed sector and ticker exposure. Filter by bill number, ticker, sector, date or event type.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

tools.name: executive_orders
tools.description: Executive orders, proclamations and memoranda with affected sectors. Any tickers are AI suggestions only (ai_suggested_tickers_unverified), never evidence of company exposure.

query.description: Words in the title or summary

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

tools.name: federal_register
tools.description: Search Federal Register documents (final rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) and the passages of their full text. Each passage carries a precise citation (FR page, CFR section and paragraph, and whether it is the rule text, proposed text, presidential text or the agency explanation). Each document carries its status and legal effect from its own dates, and coverage says what has full text. Say what a document requires, authorizes or prohibits only from the passages returned.

query.description: Words to find in the documents and their text

status.description: Status prefix, e.g. proposed, final, final: in effect

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date

until.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or before this date

parts.description: all | operative | regulatory_text | proposed_regulatory_text | presidential_text | explanation | preamble

tools.name: federal_register_document
tools.description: One Federal Register document by number: status and legal effect, its full-text passages (all, one part, one section, or those matching a query) with precise citations, the documents it cites and that cite it (exact title, FR citation or document number found in the text), and documents under the same exact RIN.

parts.description: all | operative | regulatory_text | proposed_regulatory_text | presidential_text | explanation | preamble

section.description: CFR or order section fragment, e.g. 700.34, Supplement No. 1, Sec. 3

offset.description: Skip this many passages, when a read says truncated=true

tools.name: pac_lookup
tools.description: Corporate and trade-association PACs linked to a public company (by ticker) or found by committee name, with the candidates they fund. Answers "does Lockheed have a PAC and who does it give to", "which politicians take money from Pfizer's PAC". For super PACs and mega-donors use super_pacs and money_trail instead.

tools.name: pac_totals
tools.description: Which PACs give the most: contributors to tracked candidates ranked by total dollars (FEC Schedule A), by election cycle, with donor-processing conduits like ActBlue and WinRed separated out. mode=disbursers ranks committees by their own reported disbursements instead. Use for "which PACs donate the most to Congress" questions; for super PACs use super_pacs.

cycle.description: Two-year election cycle, e.g. 2026 or 2024; omit for all

tools.name: lobbying
tools.description: Senate LDA lobbying disclosures: what a company spent lobbying, which firms it hired, which issues it worked, which agencies it contacted, which bills it named, and how many of its lobbyists previously held government posts. Or pass bill= for everyone who lobbied a given bill. This is the intent layer — super PAC money says who a company is FOR, lobbying says what it WANTS. Answers "what is Coinbase lobbying on", "who lobbied HR1234", "which agencies does Lockheed contact".

company.description: Company name; resolved by exact match

bill.description: Bill number, e.g. HR1234 or S.567 — returns everyone who lobbied it

since_year.description: Only filings from this year onward

tools.name: money_trail
tools.description: How much a person or organization gave, through which entities, to which committees, and what those committees did with it. Answers "how much did Elon Musk give to Trump", "who did Timothy Mellon fund", "where did Uline's money go". Returns donor_identity (the resolved person or organization, every employer spelling folded into one, with lifetime totals), given_via (the LLCs, trusts and partnerships the cheques were actually written under — how the money reached the committee), the recipient committees, and each super PAC's independent spending for and against candidates. Names go in as written ("Elon Musk"); the FEC form ("MUSK, ELON") is handled. Ambiguous names return matched_as; narrow with employer.

name.description: Donor: a person ("Ken Griffin") or organization ("Uline")

cycle.description: Two-year election cycle, e.g. 2024 or 2026; omit for current and previous

employer.description: Narrow to receipts whose employer field contains this (e.g. "Tesla")

tools.name: super_pacs
tools.description: Which super PACs are pulling the strings: the largest by money raised, spent or on hand for a cycle, from the FEC's own committee totals. With query or committee_id, one committee's profile: its top donors, what it spent for and against which candidates, and the vendors it paid for campaign work. With shared_vendors, the media buyers and consultancies working for more than one committee. With public_companies, listed companies ranked by the political money they give, resolved to tickers. A committee profile also names the public companies behind its money. Answers "biggest super PACs this cycle", "who funds MAGA Inc", "what is America PAC spending on", "which firms work for both sides", "which public companies give the most".

types.description: "all" to include every PAC type; default super PACs and hybrids only

shared_vendors.description: Return vendors paid by two or more committees instead of a committee ranking

min_committees.description: With shared_vendors: minimum committees sharing a vendor (default 2)

public_companies.description: Return publicly traded companies ranked by political money given, resolved to tickers

ticker.description: With public_companies: one issuer, e.g. COIN

tools.name: outside_money
tools.description: Outside money on a candidate: every super PAC and other filer spending independently to support or oppose them, with totals, from FEC Schedule E. Answers "who is backing Trump", "which groups are attacking this senator", "how much outside money is in the Ohio Senate race". Candidate names go in as written.

cycle.description: Two-year election cycle, e.g. 2024 or 2026; omit for all

tools.name: data_coverage
tools.description: Row counts and the latest dated row for every dataset behind these tools, plus entity-resolution coverage. Call it when an answer depends on how complete the data is, or before saying something does not exist.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: The themes the government is currently funding across bills, contracts, solicitations and filings, each with a permanent page and a verdict.

tools.name: get_theme
tools.description: One theme in full: the setup, the dated chronology with each beat linked to its source record, why it matters, what to watch, and the evidence.

theme_id.description: Theme id from list_themes (with or without hs:theme: prefix)

tools.name: latest_events
tools.description: The newest events across every source (awards, trades, filings, bills, orders, themes), with provenance. Optional filters by category, ticker or source id.

tools.name: track_record
tools.description: Every forward call HillSignal made since May 2025, verified against SPY 30 days later, with the inclusion rules and the miss rate.

tools.name: institutional_holders
tools.description: Largest institutional holders of a ticker from 13F-HR filings HillSignal has ingested, latest position per institution.

tools.name: foreign_agents
tools.description: Who is paid to represent a foreign government or party inside the United States, and HOW MUCH, from the Justice Department's FARA register and the contracts filed with it. Pass top="contracts" for the biggest deals — the largest contract prices, who pays whom, and who owns the client in the filer's own sworn words. Pass country= to LIST THAT COUNTRY'S AGENTS BY NAME: registered_agents is the full current roster, each with its foreign principal, registration number and dates, plus former_agents and the counts. Answer "how many agents does Israel have and who are they" from that roster. Pass bill= for the foreign interests that lobbied a bill, or nothing for the country leaderboard. A country response also carries also_in_lobbying_data, the minority of those agents that additionally file under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, split into DIRECT, where the lobbying client IS the foreign principal and bills are named, and SHARED_FIRM, where one firm holds a foreign registration and separate domestic clients — context, never a claim about those clients. That subset is never the roster. Countries are spelled as the register spells them. A country roster also carries the MONEY per agent: agreed_price is the contract price from the agreement exhibit filed at registration, always with the rate it is stated at, and reported_receipts is what the agent later reported actually receiving, as a floor rather than earnings. Both are null where no figure could be proved. Each agent may also carry foreign_principal_owned_by — the filer's sworn words on who owns the foreign principal, which is how a US-registered company names its foreign parent.

top.description: Pass "contracts" to rank the BIGGEST foreign-agent contract prices on file — who is paid the most, by whom. Combine with country= to narrow it.

rate.description: With top=contracts: the rate to rank, "month" (default) or "year", "quarter", "hour", "one-time". Rates are never mixed or converted.

country.description: Country as the register spells it, e.g. "ISRAEL", "SAUDI ARABIA", "KOREA, SOUTH"

bill.description: Bill number, e.g. HR1234 — returns foreign principals that lobbied it

tools.name: foreign_agent_filings
tools.description: Every document a FARA registrant has filed with the Justice Department, newest first: date, type, foreign principal, and a link to the filed document. Pass registration (the registration number other tools return) or firm (the registrant name as filed, matched exactly). A name on several registrations returns the list to choose from; registrations are never merged.

firm.description: Registrant name as filed, e.g. "Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP"

tools.name: patents
tools.description: Every patent HillSignal holds for a company, with the total count: patent number, owner as filed, grant date, abstract and a USPTO link, newest first. Pass ticker, or assignee (the owner's whole name, matched exactly). Answer "how many patents does T-Mobile have" from total_on_file and list them with offset paging. The set is a USPTO sample of strategic technology areas, not every patent.

assignee.description: Patent owner name as filed, e.g. "T-MOBILE INNOVATIONS LLC"

tools.name: form_d_raises
tools.description: SEC Form D private placements by issuer name, resolved ticker, date or minimum amount. No minimum size is applied: pass min_amount to impose one. A null offering_amount means the filer stated no offering size, which Form D permits, and is not a raise of zero.

since.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); only rows on or after this date
